 News Delhi High Court hears plea by Neha Bora challenging bond notice: LIVE UPDATES 
 Bora was detained on October 16 while attending a gathering at Mandi House. Two days later, Delhi Police asked them to execute a personal bond of ₹10,000 with a surety to “maintain peace during the period of inquiry." Neha Bora Bar & Bench Updated on :  22 Oct 2026, 11:45 am 
 Copied 
 Follow Us 5:44 am, 22 Oct 2026 The Delhi High Court is slated to hear All India Students Association (AISA) president Neha Bora's petition challenging a notice issued to them by a Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) directing them to execute a personal bond of ₹10,000 and maintain peace.
 Bora, who has been at the forefront of student protests and the movement against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, was detained on October 16 while attending a gathering at Mandi House. 
 They have alleged that they were taken to an undisclosed location and subsequently to RK Puram police station, where they were held overnight before being released at 6 AM the following day. 
 They received the SEM notice on October 18. The notice cites allegations of sloganeering at Mandi House, repeated protests around Jantar Mantar despite prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the BNSS, and instigating people to participate in a protest at Connaught Place.
 Bora has alleged that the proceedings amount to an attempt to curb peaceful dissent and violate their fundamental rights to freedom of speech, assembly and personal liberty.
 The matter was listed before the Court yesterday. However, Bora's counsel sought an adjournment, following which it was adjourned till today.
 Justice Subramonium Prasad is hearing the case. 
 Live updates from the hearing today feature on this page. 
 9:06 am, 22 Oct 2026 Hearing starts 
 9:07 am, 22 Oct 2026 ASG Chetan Sharma: We have objections to both maintainability and entertainability.
 9:08 am, 22 Oct 2026 Senior Advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan: It is a very narrow issue wrt to notice under Section 126 and 130 of BNSS. Petitioner is a leader of AISA and very active in public life. The facts are that over a period of time certain protests have arisen in the country as it the want against what the government does. As far as my client is concerned there has been no exhortation to violence it has been entirely peaceful.
 9:09 am, 22 Oct 2026 Gopal S: She has been asking for reforms. Over time, she has put out tweets and exhorted people to join.
 9:11 am, 22 Oct 2026 Gopal S refers to Jantar Mantar on a map.
 9:13 am, 22 Oct 2026 Bench: Your arguments are on the wordings of Section 130 and 126. 
 Gopal S: On October 15 there is a press conference by the petitioner in Press Club. On October 16 at 4 PM a post is put up. This was a reaction to the fact that Jantar Mantar was suddenly denotified.
 9:14 am, 22 Oct 2026 Gopal S: This is issued by her promising a meeting at Mandi House. What is important is what is missing from this post. There is no question of incitement to violence, breaking of any law, breach peace, upsetting public tranquility, inviting congregation in order to commit any offence.
 9:16 am, 22 Oct 2026 Gopal S: On the evening of October 16, when she called for the protest, when she goes to the Mandi House area, she comes to be detained in barely 10-15 minutes. At that time she had not been guilty of any offence. The only thing that happened was that she raised some slogans and she was detained. We believe that it is completely illegal detention.
 9:17 am, 22 Oct 2026 Gopal S: The protest at CP was organised by some other organisation. She had given a call for Mandi House. It has now become a practise that when people are protesting, they are taken away, not allowed to get in touch with lawyer, nothing.
 9:18 am, 22 Oct 2026 Gopal S: At night she was taken to RK Puram police station. No one knew about it till wee hours of the morning.
 9:18 am, 22 Oct 2026 Gopal S: The first safeguard I have is I can reach out to a lawyer or family immediately. The next day there is a qalandara submitted to SEM.
 9:19 am, 22 Oct 2026 The qalandara is being read in the court.
 9:20 am, 22 Oct 2026 Gopal S: There is no 163 there but loudspeakers are telling us that 163 is in place.
 9:25 am, 22 Oct 2026 Advocate Abhik Chimni (also appearing for Bora) is reading the qalandara.
 9:28 am, 22 Oct 2026 Gopal S: It is admitted that there was a direction by senior officers to initiate the procedure under Section 126. It is relevant because the SEM here is also an ACP.
 9:29 am, 22 Oct 2026 Gopal S: Just see the notice. It claims to be under 126 and 130 BNSS. The question is does this have substance. 
 He reads the notice issued by SEM.
 9:31 am, 22 Oct 2026 Gopal S: This is factually wrong because I did not say anything about CP. It says, "hoist the national flag without permission." I am surprised anyone can say this. No permission is needed to hoist the national flag.
 9:35 am, 22 Oct 2026 Bench: We are in pre-135. I want you to address whether what this court is doing under Article 22 of the Constitution is the job of magistrate under 135 (3) BNSS.
 9:35 am, 22 Oct 2026 Gopal S: My point is that this question of personal bond etc. does not arise at this stage until the inquiry is complete. On this we have the 7 judge bench judgement of the Supreme Court.
 9:37 am, 22 Oct 2026 Bench: Because of last three word in the notice.... The purport of the notice is please satisfy me during the period of inquiry you should not give a bond. On satisfaction the magistrate can decide... Should we go to that extent or should we confine ourselves to the notice issued under 126 and the reason behind it?
 9:38 am, 22 Oct 2026 Gopal S: First, it [notice] is cut and paste which vitiates it. Second, even for an interim bond an inquiry is essential. The magistrate could not have birthed the idea of a personal bond until the inquiry into the necessity of the bond was complete.
 9:38 am, 22 Oct 2026 Court: The First point is clear, the second I am not with you as of now.
 9:40 am, 22 Oct 2026 Gopal S (on notice) : What am I expected to say? How do I respond to this?
 9:40 am, 22 Oct 2026 Court explains the procedure. 
 Court: Tell me where you and I do not agree on this?
 9:40 am, 22 Oct 2026 Gopal S: There are a dozen judgments. I don't want to burden Justice Prasad in the middle of the vacation; that is why we have given a select few judgments.
 9:41 am, 22 Oct 2026 Gopal S takes the court to relevant sections of the BNSS.
 9:45 am, 22 Oct 2026 Gopal S: These 4 sections are important because if for example under 128 a notice is issued to a person X and assume that he is going to commit a cognisable offence... 
 Court: When you read 135, I want to know what is your input on proviso after 135 (3). Read the first proviso. How do you see 135... I am saying this in your favour. How do you read this proviso in respect to what is being transpired now?
 9:46 am, 22 Oct 2026 Court: As I told Abhik yesterday, is it not better for you to 135 inquiry to be completed?
 9:46 am, 22 Oct 2026 Court: Therefore, again, is it not more prudent for you to wait till this is over. And then hit this court on Saturday to trouble me on a Sunday.
 9:47 am, 22 Oct 2026 Court: The subjective satisfaction I cannot go into unless the subjective satisfaction is such that... The compass is exceedingly narrow.
 9:48 am, 22 Oct 2026 Gopal S: The notice is ex facie constitutionally wrong and legally wrong.
 9:50 am, 22 Oct 2026 Court: So your third argument would be no independent opinion of the SEM? 
 Gopal S: Yes, in fact, there is no opinion at all.
 9:51 am, 22 Oct 2026 Gopal S refers to Section 135 BNSS.
 9:51 am, 22 Oct 2026 Gopal S: Stage 1 is substance; stage 2 is the inquiry.
 9:56 am, 22 Oct 2026 Gopal S refers to 7 judge Supreme Court bench in Madhu Limaye case.
 10:06 am, 22 Oct 2026 Gopal S (relying on the judgement) : The hearsay which has formed the substratum of 126 [BNSS] becomes the basis for you to conduct an inquiry and give reasons in writing under 130 [BNSS]. Constitution Bench makes it clear that at every stage you have to give reasons in writing.
 10:07 am, 22 Oct 2026 Gopal S refers to Section 107 of the CrPC of 1898. 
 Gopal S: There is no bond question arising at the show cause notice stage.
 10:09 am, 22 Oct 2026 Court: The question is that could it (show cause notice) be in the nature of a judgement? The question is why should the court go into whether the opinion arrived at this stage...
 10:10 am, 22 Oct 2026 Court: Your argument is that it is a mechanical cut paste? 
 Gopal S: There is a whisper from the other side; if he keeps his issue about maintainability, then I will have to argue more on that. 
 Court: He is saying it is premature.
 10:12 am, 22 Oct 2026 Court: ASG sir, he is addressing the merits and maintainability together. 
 Court (in lighter vein) : Gopal doesn't come here often. You know this court doesn't believe in timelines... 
 Gopal S: When I do come here and I am engaged like this, it is refreshing.
 10:13 am, 22 Oct 2026 Gopal S: If I were to engage with the merits of the allegations, then my remedy is obviously not here. I am not engaging. I am saying compliance with law. That entitles me to come here under 226.
 10:17 am, 22 Oct 2026 Gopal S refers to judgements.
 10:18 am, 22 Oct 2026 He now refers to 2018 Delhi High Court judgement in Aldanish Rein vs State Of Nct Of Delhi & Anr.
 10:22 am, 22 Oct 2026 Gopal S says he will hand over a note to the court. 
 Court: Note? I have to give my judgement tomorrow no?
 10:23 am, 22 Oct 2026 Court is informed that the next date of hearing before SEM court is Saturday.
 10:26 am, 22 Oct 2026 Gopal S: Before I end, I will draw my lordship's attention to article 19(1)a) and 19(1)(b). What is common in all these is "public order".
 10:28 am, 22 Oct 2026 Gopal S concludes.
 10:32 am, 22 Oct 2026 ASG Chetan Sharma begins his submissions. 
 Court: What is your reaction to 135 proviso "a" as to whether this wherein a bond is to be given from 127, 128 and 129, whether at the time when magistrate... Though your notice says... Second point I want your argument on is other than qalandara was there any other material or inquiry done by you to substantiate your opinion under 130 leaving to show cause notice. These are two events, one legal and one factual. After that you start.
 10:33 am, 22 Oct 2026 ASG Sharma takes the court through the BNSS provisions.
 10:35 am, 22 Oct 2026 Court: Let's assume someone tells the magistrate that x was there shouting slogans... And on that basis, he issues a 126 BNSS notice. So therefore, without making an inquiry, he gives a 126 notice to file a bond without even finding out that 'x' may not even be there at all and on that very date there are press reports that 'x' was at some other place giving a speech; then is it not necessary for the magistrate to do an independent search that the information received is credible enough to take an action?
 10:37 am, 22 Oct 2026 Court: Also, when the hearing is to be held, will these documents be supplied to the other side? Because it forms the basis of the opinion. 
 ASG Sharma: Yes. I am duty bound today, while representing the State to take your lordships to what I call is the sine qua non of the eye of the needle that my lordships point. Two things need to be keep in mind. The entire argument proceeds on two aspects. One, procedurally there is no challenge. His case is 130, the requirements in 130 and 126 do not meet. So it is a challenge to the substance, not the procedure.
 10:38 am, 22 Oct 2026 ASG Sharma: The challenge to 130 is based on demurrer that there are some penal consequences...
 10:40 am, 22 Oct 2026 Court: According to you, receipt of information "likely to commit"?
 ASG Sharma: Likely to commit what? Not the crime in traditional sense but a breach of peace and that may probably occasion a breach... This has some connotation... This is subjective satisfaction as wide it can get.
 10:41 am, 22 Oct 2026 Court: "Likely to commit" is based on the information received... The question is, is there an application of mind that the information received leads to a subjective satisfaction that there is "likely to commit".
 10:42 am, 22 Oct 2026 ASG Sharma now refers to Section 130 of BNSS.
 10:48 am, 22 Oct 2026 ASG Sharma: Section 135 proviso "a" will not trump the latter part of Section 130. 
 Court: The 130 notice when you are clubbing 130 and 126, in a 130 order, that will not mean the magistrate has made a premeditated mind?
 10:50 am, 22 Oct 2026 Court: In a matter where liberty is under challenge, the only safeguard available to a citizen is the procedure, the requirement. The only safeguard is the requirement of the law to be met.
 10:52 am, 22 Oct 2026 ASG Sharma: The sine qua none of 126, in my humble submission 126 and 130 ride together. They are not disjunctive.
 10:53 am, 22 Oct 2026 ASG Sharma: If there is a likelihood that somebody may commit breach of peace, 126 BNSS kicks in with 130 BNSS. They can't be disjoined. Such technical splitting will take away the essence of public tranquillity and breach of peace. Therefore, sometimes the law enjoins you.
 10:54 am, 22 Oct 2026 ASG Sharma refers to the notice. 
 ASG Sharma: The magistrate says I have inspected the qalandara and that after inspection of qalandara, notice be issued. 
 Court: Other than qalandara, is there any other material with you?
 10:55 am, 22 Oct 2026 Court: ASG Sir, just a small request, we will require a bit more time to write the judgment. Saturday, Sunday I am not in station, the hearing will finish today. I will write the judgment by Tuesday. The only request is till Tuesday, hold your hands.
 10:56 am, 22 Oct 2026 Gopal S: It does not sound good that a court is seeking adjournment. I will take in on myself that we are seeking adjournment.
 10:58 am, 22 Oct 2026 ASG Sharma: The cases against... Complete, abject, rampant violations, one after another, 12 times.
 11:01 am, 22 Oct 2026 ASG Sharma: Your lordships will see. Chapter and verse, with such material and kindly see item 11 and 12. Everything is in full public view. A person who is in Alice in Wonderland will say I have received this out of the blue. Please see serial number 11 and 12. Join sitting with CJP leaders and Prashant Bhushan where it was said, "ye regime change ki ladai hai aur ham regime change karwa ke rahenge" (this fight is for a regime change and we will make the regime change) . She was part of the same gathering.
 11:03 am, 22 Oct 2026 Gopal S: There is nothing wrong with regime change in a democracy. 
 Court: Do we need to go into that? 
 ASG Sharma: Regime change will happen by votes not by lumpen elements congregating in New Delhi.
 11:04 am, 22 Oct 2026 ASG Sharma: The law allows us to have conjoint 126 and 130. There is a likelihood of breach of peace. Don't leave it to a technicality... All mayhem may have broken loose in the capital of the city. Because this is preventive in nature so that law would land its weight to the way parliament envisaged it to be.
 11:04 am, 22 Oct 2026 ASG Sharma: They are asking you to sit in the armchair of magistrate and substitute your opinion to that of the magistrate... He [magistrate] has not formed an opinion yet. He only says for peace and tranquility, will your or won't you give a bond. Is this petition a reply to the show cause given by the SEM? The answer is no.
 11:07 am, 22 Oct 2026 ASG Sharma: It [notice] has not resulted in bond or penal consequences. It has in fact, said that you can come in person or through counsel. She sought an application. 
 Court: Can they send a lawyer to represent? 
 ASG Sharma: Yes. 
 Gopal S: I had moved an application seeking exemption from personal appearance.
 11:08 am, 22 Oct 2026 ASG Sharma: She has to do two things, she can come with lawyer, not come with the lawyer or send a lawyer but breach of peace is the main concern in the mind of the government. Bond to dena padega (Bond will have to be given).
 11:09 am, 22 Oct 2026 Court: Should we take a two minute tea break?
 Bench rises. 
 11:13 am, 22 Oct 2026 Court asks Gopal S to consider if he would like to continue on this petition or wait till the show cause notice is over.
 11:16 am, 22 Oct 2026 Bench reassembles. 
 Hearing starts. 
 11:18 am, 22 Oct 2026 ASG Sharma refers to the qalandara again.
 11:21 am, 22 Oct 2026 ASG Sharma: The question was if the SEM has applied his mind... There is a definite source. There is GD entry, past FIR and offences, the situation on the streets and IO is called. Magistrate asked the IO to explain. It was like a hearing.
 11:23 am, 22 Oct 2026 ASG Sharma now refers to Section 129 (e) of the BNSS.
 11:25 am, 22 Oct 2026 Court: The concern of the petitioner is that he has already been branded as a bad boy, and I am now being made to promise that I will be a good boy. When a person comes to the court that I promise to behave properly, it means that they are not behaving properly.
 11:26 am, 22 Oct 2026 Court: It is the stigma the person has which has led to this proceeding. It has a facet in Article 21. 
 ASG Sharma: When there are 6 FIRs against are a paragon of innocence?
 11:27 am, 22 Oct 2026 Court: Here is a person who is being made to give a bond of good behaviour pending an inquiry. It is like suspension till inquiry.
 11:29 am, 22 Oct 2026 ASG Sharma now refers to judgements.
 11:34 am, 22 Oct 2026 ASG Sharma: Their argument that their call was only for Mandi House and not CP and that no 163 BNSS was in force is false. There was 163 BNSS. Police was outnumbered, she ran. She dodges. She was stopped, she did not stop. She ran towards CP.
 11:38 am, 22 Oct 2026 Court: One promise ASG sir, all documents you have given to me will be handed over to her.
 11:38 am, 22 Oct 2026 ASG Sharma: It will be done.
 11:39 am, 22 Oct 2026 ASG Sharma concludes. 
 Gopal S begins his rejoinder arguments.
 11:42 am, 22 Oct 2026 Court reserves verdict. 
 Justice Prasad: Order tomorrow at 6PM.
 11:44 am, 22 Oct 2026 Hearing over
